waypoints.name: Ofenpass approach
waypoints.advice: You top out at 2149 m here. The road climbs 1556 m on the way up to it, steadily. At this height the road is a summer one: snow gates can stay shut into June and shut again in October. Next is Pordoi Pass.

waypoints.name: Pordoi Pass
waypoints.advice: 2239 m, and the road stops climbing. Nothing on this route is higher. Next is Campolongo Pass, mostly downhill.

waypoints.name: Campolongo Pass
waypoints.advice: The high point of this section, 1875 m up. You lose 364 m on the way down to it, steadily. High enough to hold ice in the shaded corners early and late in the year. Next is Gardena Pass, climbing 261 m.

waypoints.name: Gardena Pass
waypoints.advice: Gardena Pass tops the climb at 2136 m. The road climbs 261 m on the way up to it, steadily. Next is Val Gardena overnight base, mostly downhill.

waypoints.name: Val Gardena overnight base
waypoints.advice: Val Gardena overnight base comes up 397 km in. You lose 576 m on the way down to it, steadily. Next is Back to Chur, mostly downhill.

waypoints.name: Back to Chur
waypoints.advice: Back to Chur closes the day. You lose 967 m on the way down to it, steadily. Next is Glarus valley fuel, mostly downhill.

waypoints.name: Glarus valley fuel

waypoints.name: Klausenpass

scenicChapters.title: Timmelsjoch High Alpine Road
scenicChapters.narrative: Height already gained and held. The road stays near 2239 m for 216 km instead of surrendering it to the next valley — exposed ground: wind matters more here than gradient. Nothing blocks it.

scenicChapters.title: Great Dolomites Road
scenicChapters.narrative: The last of the trees go and the road runs out onto open ground. The summit sits at 2136 m, and what surrounds it is rock, weather and distance. Cold comes early up here and stays late. Ride it with something in reserve: the summit is not the end of the work, only the middle of it.
scenicChapters.riderNote: Check the pass is open before you commit to it.

scenicChapters.title: Stelvio Pass
scenicChapters.narrative: This is where a day makes up time without anyone trying. Third and fourth, and very little else. 313 km that neither climbs nor drops much. The road settles into the ground rather than fighting it.

scenicChapters.title: Klausen Pass
scenicChapters.narrative: For 46 km this is Klausen Pass, a road with a name of its own and a reason for it — expect company on a summer weekend. Early is better than fast.
scenicChapters.riderNote: Check the pass is open before you commit to it.

scenicChapters.title: Pragel and Ibergeregg Loop
scenicChapters.narrative: Water arrives beside the road and stays for 53 km. The line follows the shore because there is nowhere else for it to go. Slow enough to look. The surface follows the shoreline, so the corners arrive where the water decided, not where an engineer did.

dolomites-sella-ronda-overnight-scout-an.story: From Chur it runs 899 km to Glarus; allow about 17 h 53 of riding. The climbs: Ofenpass approach, Pordoi Pass, Campolongo Pass and Gardena Pass. It tops out at about 2,250 m. Klausen Pass is subject to seasonal closure - check it is open before you set off. It crosses from Switzerland into Italy - carry ID and check vignette or toll rules. The passes are the reason to go.
